title: Automated Architectural Rendering Pipeline
business: Architectural firms requiring high-fidelity 3D model rendering for client presentations.
problem: Local workstations fail to process complex 3D scenes within required deadlines, leading to project bottlenecks and hardware underutilization.
solution: Azure Batch provides a managed service to create and manage pools of compute nodes, enabling the parallel execution of rendering tasks across multiple virtual machines.
steps: Define a Batch Account to serve as the central management entity for compute resources.
Configure a Pool of compute nodes specifying the virtual machine size and operating system image.
Create a Job to act as a logical container for the collection of rendering tasks.
Submit individual rendering Tasks to the job, each referencing specific scene files and output requirements.
Monitor task execution and retrieve rendered assets from linked storage once completion is signaled.
outcome: The firm achieves consistent, predictable rendering timelines by scaling compute resources dynamically to match the volume of pending 3D scenes.
limitation: Azure Batch manages the infrastructure but does not automatically handle complex application-level dependency conflicts; verify compatibility by checking node startup task logs.

By providing a pre-configured workstation environment for every architect.
By eliminating the need for storage accounts during the rendering process.
